State Management and Persistence

All process state in TaktX is managed in Kafka Streams state stores. This includes process instances, variables, timers, and message subscriptions.

Partitioned State

State is partitioned by key (such as process instance ID), allowing for distributed processing and storage. Each engine node is responsible for a subset of the state, based on partition assignment.

In-Memory vs. Persisted Stores

State stores can be configured for in-memory (fast, volatile) or persisted (durable, larger) storage. This flexibility allows deployments to be tuned for specific performance and durability requirements.

Changelogs and Recovery

All state changes are logged to Kafka changelogs. If a node fails, its state can be restored from the changelog, ensuring durability and consistency.

Data Retention and Log Compaction

A common misconception is that Kafka only retains data for a fixed period (such as a few days or weeks), after which it is deleted. While Kafka does support time-based retention, TaktX relies on Kafka's log compaction feature for critical state. Log compaction ensures that for each key (such as a process instance ID), only the most recent value is retained, and older, superseded records are removed. This means that state is not lost by accident: as long as a key is still relevant, its latest value remains available in the log.

Data is only deleted from a compacted topic when it has lost its purpose—such as when a process instance is completed and no longer needed. This approach provides strong guarantees against accidental data loss, while keeping storage requirements manageable. Operators can tune compaction and retention policies to match their business and compliance needs.
